Just read Industrial Society and Its Future, which is itself a summation of his points. Some of his more famous ideas include:
>technological society cannot be tamed by human rationality; if left unchecked it will lead to a mass collapse and our best bet is to pull the plug on technological growth since the alternative (letting it go unchecked) would lead to an even bigger catastrophe
>the tech. society goes against human dignity (which especially pertains to potential future innovations) and obstructs what he calls the "power process" in the favor of "surrogate activities"
>leftists claim to rebel against the system but in fact unknowingly work for it and help it grow, and they're insecure, oversocialized and indicative of mass insanity
>Conservatives say they're traditionalists but in practice mindlessly welcome every tech. innovation
>the good parts of tech. growth can't be separated from the bad ones
